paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus prayed for YOU. Before He went to the cross, He prayed for the disciples, and then He said He was not asking on behalf of them alone, "but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message" (John 17:20). That's every baker who has ever believed because somebody passed the message along. I spent years in a junk drawer thinking nobody was thinking of me, and here Jesus is, thinking of His people before they even existed.

Now look at what He asks for. He doesn't ask the Father to take them out of the world, but "that You keep them from the evil one" (John 17:15). He asks the Father to sanctify them by the truth and says "Your word is truth" (John 17:17), so the Word isn't a side snack, friend, and that's why I keep inviting bakers back to my ovens. He also says eternal life is this: knowing "the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent" (John 17:3).

And the prayer ends with love, because that's where it's been going the whole time. Jesus prays that His people would be one, so "that the world may believe that You sent Me" (John 17:21). He wants them with Him, seeing His glory, and He wants the Father's love for Him to be in them (John 17:24, 26). So when you feel small, or forgotten, or a little worn around the edges like me, remember that you are prayed for and loved.
